title: How I created an AI game in under 5 minutes using Gemini + free AI game generator (Mobile & Web)
author: Funny-You-2062
selftext:
Wanted to share a quick workflow test on how to create an AI game without writing manual code, using Gemini as the designer and a free builder platform for execution.

**The Workflow:**

1. **Gemini for Design:** I pitched my airship shooter idea to Gemini to outline the visual layout, control scheme, and mechanics.
2. **Execution:** I fed that prompt structure into Klipy (a free AI game generator) to handle the engine, rendering, and logic.
3. **Result:** In under 5 minutes, it compiled a working 3D AI game (*Sky-Pirate Arsenal*).

Attached a video from mobile showing gameplay. It features working altitude sliders, steam pressure meters, radar, and dual port/starboard cannons targeting incoming drone waves. Even though the video is from mobile, it's fully playable in any web browser.

**Observations on AI game development:**

* Having Gemini set strict HUD constraints beforehand made the generator output much cleaner.
* Hitboxes and multi-control UI elements compiled surprisingly well out of the box.
* Juggling altitude sliders and side-cannon buttons on a phone screen takes a minute to get used to.

**Looking for recommendations & tips:**

* **Prompting:** How are you structuring prompts in Gemini to get tighter mechanics for AI game creation?
* **Mobile UI:** Any advice on making multi-button HUD layouts feel smoother on mobile touchscreens?

*(Playable web link in comments)*
